domains.name: 8. Business Continuity Plan Exercise/Test, Assessment, and Maintenance
10. Coordination with External Agencies and Resources

domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers establishing the need for a business continuity program within an organization. Candidates learn to secure management leadership, define program scope, organize resources, and establish governance policies required to support ongoing operational resilience and organizational stability.

Risk assessment focuses on identifying threats, vulnerabilities, and potential operational disruptions. Candidates evaluate likelihood and potential impacts to prioritize mitigation actions, establishing baseline controls to protect key organizational assets and maintain critical functions during various types of emergencies.

This area emphasizes quantifying the qualitative and quantitative impacts of operational disruptions over time. Practitioners analyze critical business functions, recovery time objectives, and recovery point objectives necessary to prioritize system restoration across all organizational units and departments.

Candidates explore methods for determining effective recovery strategies for operations and technology. Focus areas include evaluating alternative resources, processing facilities, third-party vendor support, and cost-benefit options to ensure seamless continuity following an unexpected disruption to the business environment.

This domain focuses on structuring emergency response procedures and immediate actions during an event. Topics include establishing incident command structures, life safety management, emergency evacuation plans, and immediate operational stabilization techniques during severe organizational crises or unexpected events.

Focusing on operationalizing continuity strategies, this subject addresses drafting formal business continuity plans. Candidates study techniques for documenting action procedures, defining roles, establishing communication pathways, and distributing plans to critical operational personnel effectively to ensure organizational readiness.

Creating a culture of business continuity requires formal education and awareness initiatives. Candidates learn to design, implement, and assess training programs tailored to staff levels, ensuring personnel understand their specific responsibilities during operational disruptions and emergency response scenarios.

This subject addresses evaluating continuity plans through systematic testing and exercises. Candidates study exercise design, objective setting, performance evaluation, post-exercise reporting, and continuous plan updates to maintain alignment with changing organizational requirements and evolving threat landscapes over time.

Crisis communications involves managing information flow during an emergency. Candidates learn to develop communication strategies, identify key stakeholders, manage media relations, and ensure accurate, timely information reaches employees and the public to maintain organizational reputation and trust.

Coordination with external agencies ensures effective collaboration during large-scale incidents. Candidates study how to integrate with public safety, government entities, and private sector partners to leverage shared resources and maintain compliance with regulatory requirements during complex recovery operations.

editorial.overview: The Certified Business Continuity Professional (CBCP) examination administered by DRI International evaluates professional knowledge across business continuity planning and management practices. Candidates are tested on subject matter spanning 10 core domains, including program management, risk assessment, and crisis communications. The assessment features a total duration of 150 minutes, and candidates must achieve a minimum passing score of 75% to successfully demonstrate proficiency. Earning this designation confirms an individual's capability to design, implement, and maintain effective business continuity and disaster recovery frameworks within organizational contexts.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Effective preparation for the test requires systematically reviewing all 10 Professional Practices established by DRI International. Candidates should dedicate study time to core topics such as Business Impact Analysis and Business Continuity Strategies. Practicing sample scenario questions under timed conditions helps candidate stamina during the 150 minutes exam session. Candidates must also target a clear understanding of all concepts to reliably secure a mark above the 75% passing threshold.
skills_summary: Developing organizational program management frameworks for business continuity.
Conducting risk assessments and business impact analyses.
Formulating strategies for business continuity and operational recovery.
Establishing incident preparedness and response procedures.
Designing and facilitating training and awareness programs.
Executing crisis communications and coordinating with external resources.
editorial.who_should_take: This certification is designed for business continuity planners, risk managers, disaster recovery specialists, and emergency management professionals seeking formal validation of their expertise. Applicants should possess experience in establishing and maintaining operational resilience programs across complex corporate or public sector environments.
